claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to gather some information about your circumstances and the children you're responsible for.

Let me start with my first question:

**How many children are you responsible for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm responsible for one child - my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 17 years old, there are some specific rules that apply. Let me ask you a follow-up question:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as school, college, university, or an apprenticeship)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's just started an apprenticeship actually. He's training to be an electrician.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. I need to clarify one important detail about Alex's apprenticeship:

**Is Alex doing his apprenticeship in England?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. We live here in England and his apprenticeship is with a local electrical company.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have one more important question to complete my assessment:

**Are you currently living in the UK, and are you the one with day-to-day responsibility for Alex (for example, you live with him or you're making financial contributions towards his upkeep)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And yes, Alex lives at home with me, so I have day-to-day responsibility for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility. Let me review the rules carefully:

According to the Child Benefit rules:
- You normally qualify if you're responsible for a child under 16 and live in the UK
- For children aged 16 or over, you can usually still qualify if they're under 20 and stay in approved education or training
- However, if your child starts an **apprenticeship in England**, Child Benefit payments will stop

Since Alex has just started an apprenticeship in England, this means you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for him, as apprenticeships in England are specifically excluded from the approved education or training that would allow continued Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**. 

The reason is that while Child Benefit can normally continue for young people aged 16-19 who remain in approved education or training, apprenticeships in England are specifically excluded from this. The rules state that you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts an apprenticeship in England.

If you have any questions about this decision or believe your circumstances are different, you can contact HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) Child Benefit Office for further guidance.

While Child Benefit can continue for 16-19 year olds in approved education or training, the rules specifically state that you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child 'starts an apprenticeship in England'. Therefore, Alex's apprenticeship disqualifies him from Child Benefit eligibility.
